findings.title: process.kill() now gated behind a broken isinstance check, preventing restart of hung/crashed processes
findings.body: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the call to `process.kill()` is now wrapped in `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process):`. However, processes are created via `self.mp_context.Process` with a 'spawn' context (`multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process`), which returns a `SpawnProcess` instance. `SpawnProcess` does NOT subclass `multiprocessing.Process` (the default context's Process class) — both only share a common base `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`. Therefore `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False for the actual spawned worker processes, and `kill()` is silently skipped. Previously (pre-PR) `process.kill()` was called unconditionally (wrapped only in try/except ValueError), so it worked correctly. With this change, hung or crashed flusher processes are never actually killed before a replacement process is spawned to handle the same shards, leading to zombie/leaked processes that may still be alive and could continue producing to Kafka or interacting with Redis concurrently with the new process for the same shards — risking duplicate segment production and resource leaks.

findings.title: Dead code: unused `_create_process_for_shard` method
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) is defined but never called anywhere in the class; `_create_process_for_shards` (plural) is used instead throughout. This leftover method should be removed to avoid confusion.

findings.title: Inconsistent metrics tag key between related timers
findings.body: The `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` timer uses tag key `"shard"` while the nearly-identical `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer uses tag key `"shards"` (plural) for the same value (a comma-joined shard list). This inconsistency fragments metrics dashboards/queries that expect a single consistent tag name across these two closely related timers.
